title: ⚡ Skimming — Read for Structure, Not Detail

sections.heading: What skimming means
sections.body:
Skimming = reading the FIRST SENTENCE of each paragraph only. You get the topic map of the passage without reading everything.

Goal: In 60 seconds, know:
• What is the overall topic?
• How many paragraphs are there?
• What is each paragraph roughly about?

This is NOT detailed reading. You are building a mental map.

sections.heading: Why it works
sections.body: Academic texts always begin paragraphs with the main idea (the topic sentence). If you read only first sentences, you capture ~70% of the content structure in 15% of the time.

highlight: Never start reading the whole passage first. Skim → read questions → scan. This order saves 8–10 minutes per test.

example.wrong: Reading every word of the passage before looking at the questions.
example.right: Read first sentences only (60 sec) → read all questions → scan for specific answers using keywords.

title: 🔍 Scanning — Finding Information Fast
body:
Scanning = searching for SPECIFIC information without reading everything.

How to scan:
1. Identify 2–3 keywords from the question
2. Move your eyes quickly down the passage
3. Slow down ONLY when you see a keyword or its synonym
4. Read that sentence + the one before and after

Critical: Questions use SYNONYMS — never the exact passage words.
Question says 'children' → passage says 'young people'
Question says 'increase' → passage says 'rise / grow / expand'

quick.label: Scan for MEANING, not identical words
Move your eyes quickly — don't read

question: What is the correct order of steps in the IELTS Reading approach?
options: Read questions first → then read the whole passage
Skim passage (60 sec) → read all questions → scan for answers
Scan passage → skim questions → read for detail
correct: Skim passage (60 sec) → read all questions → scan for answers
explanation:
✅ Correct order:
1. SKIM (60 sec): first sentences only → get structure
2. READ QUESTIONS: know what you're looking for
3. SCAN: search for keywords → slow down only at the right section

❌ Reading everything first wastes 10+ minutes and causes panic.
❌ Questions first without any passage knowledge means you don't know where to look.
hint: You read the passage FIRST — but only the first sentence of each paragraph.

question: A question asks about 'the economic consequences of urbanisation.' Which part of the passage should you scan for?
options: Paragraphs where 'economic', 'financial', 'costs', or 'benefits' appear near words for 'cities' or 'urban areas'
correct: Paragraphs where 'economic', 'financial', 'costs', or 'benefits' appear near words for 'cities' or 'urban areas'
explanation:
Scanning for SYNONYMS of your keywords is essential.

'Economic consequences' → synonyms: financial impact, costs, monetary effects, fiscal results
'Urbanisation' → synonyms: urban migration, city growth, movement to cities

Scan for ANY of these — not just the exact phrase from the question.
hint: Think: what SYNONYMS might the passage use for 'economic' and 'urbanisation'?

title: ⏱️ Time Management in IELTS Reading
body:
60 minutes. 40 questions. 3 passages.

Recommended time split:
Passage 1 (easiest): 17 minutes
Passage 2 (medium): 20 minutes
Passage 3 (hardest): 23 minutes

For EACH passage:
• 60 seconds: skim
• 2 minutes: read all questions
• Remaining time: scan and answer

If stuck on a question: SKIP and return. Never spend more than 90 seconds on one question.

quick.label: Stuck? Mark it, move on, return later
No penalty for wrong answers — always guess

question: You have 3 minutes left and 4 questions unanswered. What should you do?
options: Leave them blank — guessing is dishonest
Carefully read the passage to find each answer
Quickly scan for each answer; write your best guess for any you cannot find in time
Spend all 3 minutes on the first unanswered question
correct: Quickly scan for each answer; write your best guess for any you cannot find in time
explanation:
IELTS has NO negative marking — a wrong answer = 0 marks, same as a blank.
Therefore: always guess rather than leave blank.

With 3 minutes and 4 questions:
• ~40 seconds per question maximum
• Quick scan for each; if not found in 40 sec → write a plausible guess
• Never sacrifice 3 questions to spend 3 minutes on 1
hint: No penalty for wrong answers. A blank is guaranteed zero. A guess has a chance.

question: Which approach best demonstrates Band 8+ reading technique?
options: Reading every word carefully to ensure full understanding before answering
Answering questions in the order they appear without checking the passage
Skimming the structure, predicting where answers will be, then scanning with synonyms in mind
Reading the passage three times to memorise the content
correct: Skimming the structure, predicting where answers will be, then scanning with synonyms in mind
explanation:
Band 8 readers are STRATEGIC:
✅ They skim first — mental map of structure
✅ They predict where answers will be (Q1 is usually in Para A-B, Q10 in Para D-E)
✅ They scan using synonyms — not matching exact words
✅ They manage time deliberately

❌ Careful word-by-word reading = runs out of time
❌ Memorising = impossible and pointless for the questions asked
